name: Norethandrolone (Nilevar)

lead: Norethandrolone (Nilevar) is an oral 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesized by G. D. Searle in 1953 and introduced as an anabolic steroid in 1956, the first marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic from androgenic effects. It is cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner of later mass-building steroids.

It was prescribed for muscle wasting, burns, trauma and some aplastic anemias. It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity, and Wikipedia reports aromatase converts it to ethylestradiol. Human weight-gain data come from mid-century studies of underweight patients, including a 1959 study, and it has not been studied for appearance in modern trials.

paras: It was prescribed orally as a medicine in the 1950s and 60s. It is reported to be available today only in France.

Cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and bile canalicular changes were reported in treated patients in 1959 and 1960 papers. It was withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s over liver concerns and is Schedule III in the US.

angle.text: Norethandrolone, an early oral anabolic steroid from the 1950s, promotes nitrogen retention and protein gain, which is why it is cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner for more muscle and body weight. A 1959 weight-gain study is the main human data point.

lead: Norethandrolone (brand names Nilevar and Pronabol) is a synthetic, orally taken androgen and anabolic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group, a 17α-ethyl derivative of nandrolone. G. D. Searle synthesized it in 1953, initially as a progestin, and introduced it medically as an anabolic steroid in 1956. Wikipedia describes it as the first anabolic steroid marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic and androgenic effects. [1]

It was used for muscle wasting, severe burns, trauma and certain aplastic anemias, and was studied for male hormonal contraception. It was sold in the US in the late 1950s as Nilevar and discontinued there in the 1960s because of limited sales, and was withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s over concerns about liver damage including cholestatic jaundice. [1]

Early clinical papers reported cholestasis and peliosis hepatis in treated patients. [2][3][4] Later, a French randomized trial examined low-dose norethandrolone in elderly acute myeloid leukemia. [5] No modern trials of norethandrolone for appearance have been found. [1]
infobox: Schedule III (US); Schedule IV (Canada); available only in France per Wikipedia

paras: Norethandrolone was used for muscle wasting, severe burns, physical trauma and certain forms of aplastic anemia. [1] A 1959 American Journal of Medicine series evaluated it over six months in underweight persons, with companion papers examining liver function and bromsulphalein retention. [6] A 1967 study reported effects of norethandrolone on the anticoagulant response to bishydroxycoumarin. [7]

Norethandrolone is an androgen receptor agonist. Wikipedia states that in rodents its androgenic-to-anabolic ratio is about 1:1 to 1:2, that aromatase converts it to ethylestradiol, and that it has strong progestogenic activity. [1] A 1977 rat liver study found that norethandrolone, unlike norethindrone and ethynyloestradiol, did not cause loss of cytochrome P-450 in vitro. [8]

Papers from 1959 and 1960 reported cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and electron microscopic changes in bile canaliculi in people and rats given norethandrolone. [2][3][9] Wikipedia notes that, as with other 17α-alkylated steroids, long-term high-dose use may cause elevated liver enzymes and cirrhosis. [1]

Wikipedia lists masculinizing effects such as acne, increased hair growth, voice changes and increased sexual desire, and estrogenic effects including fluid retention, breast tenderness and gynecomastia in men. [1] A forensic and rabbit study compared heart lesions in athletes with a history of anabolic steroid abuse to lesions induced by norethandrolone in rabbits. [4]

Wikipedia says it has been used to improve physique and performance and that non-medical use is generally illicit. It is Class C5 in Brazil, Schedule IV in Canada and Schedule III in the US. [1] Analytical work has examined its transformation products in veal feces in the context of boldenone testing. [10]

A 1959 six-month evaluation in underweight persons examined liver function and bromsulphalein retention alongside weight effects. [6] A French randomized phase III trial (NCT00700544, 330 participants, started 2002) in elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia tested adding androgens, including norethandrolone, after induction therapy; the GOELAMS report found improved survival with androgen addition. [5][11] No studies of norethandrolone for appearance outcomes in healthy people were found.

timeline.event: Synthesized by G. D. Searle, initially as a progestin. [1]
Introduced medically as an anabolic steroid. [1]
Reports of cholestasis and a six-month evaluation in underweight persons are published. [2][6]

GOELAMS study reports improved survival with added androgens in elderly AML. [5]
